Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

closely adverb

tightly, near, in close union

also tightly, tight (hold tight), close together, closely linked, as close as possible

classical

Plaut. Epid. 5.2.29: artē conligā (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 6.8: artē dīligere (Lewis & Short)

artē

adverb

closely, tightly, fast

Of binding, holding and packing close: artē conligāre, to tie tight; artius conlocāre, to set closer together (Sallust). Of affection, artē dīligere, to love dearly (Pliny); of sleep, “soundly”: artē dormīre (Cic. Div. 1.59). All from Lewis & Short.

Other words

  • proximē — very close, next to; quam proximē, as close as possible

    adverb: the superlative of prope · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.14.3: proximē Pompejum sedēbam (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 6.5.3: exercitum habēre quam proximē hostem (Lewis & Short)

    Of place, “right next to, closest to”, with the accusative or dative; with quam, “as close as possible”. Of time it means “most recently, last” (Lewis & Short).

  • conjūnctē — closely, in close friendship

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 6.9.1 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Lael. 2: conjūnctissimē (Lewis & Short)

    Of people who live on close terms, conjūnctē vīvere (Nepos; Lewis & Short). In Cicero it is also “jointly, together with”.

Examples

  • artē conligā

    tie (his hands) tightPlaut. Epid. 5.2.29 (Lewis & Short)

  • proximē Pompejum sedēbam

    I was sitting right next to PompeyCic. Att. 1.14.3 (Lewis & Short)

  • exercitum habēre quam proximē hostem

    to keep the army as close to the enemy as possibleCic. Att. 6.5.3 (Lewis & Short)

See also near, firmly, carefully.
